item.title: Hardik Pandya leaves Mumbai Indians: Franchise shares goodbye message
item.description: NEW DELHI: Mumbai Indians have shared a special message for Hardik Pandya after the all-rounder moved to Punjab Kings (PBKS) ahead of the 2027 Indian Premier League (IPL) season. "Thank you, Hardik, for representing the Blue and Gold with passion and pride. We wish you the best for the journey ahead," Mumbai Indians wrote on their social media handle. Pandya has moved to Punjab Kings for Rs 18 crore in a player trade. In return, PBKS have sent fast bowler Arshdeep Singh to Mumbai Indians. According to an IPL statement, Pandya's new fee is higher than his previous salary of Rs 16.35 crore. Arshdeep, meanwhile, will continue to earn Rs 18 crore, the same amount he received at PBKS. Pandya ends second stint with Mumbai Indians The move brings an end to Pandya's second stint with Mumbai Indians. He won four IPL titles with the franchise. Pandya first joined MI in 2015 and played an important role in their title wins in 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020 with his performances with both bat and ball. He returned to the team in 2024 and took over as captain from Rohit Sharma. However, Mumbai Indians struggled during this period. In 162 IPL matches, Pandya has scored 2,955 runs at a strike rate of 146.28. He has also taken 82 wickets. item.title: FAMU football QB Isaiah Knowles turns 'what-if' into lasting impact
item.description: Isaiah Knowles’ daily routine looks quite different nowadays. Instead of suiting up as Florida A&M’s starting quarterback , the graduate student is now holding a practice itinerary, teaching, and observing the offense from the sidelines during games. “Man, I wish I was able to play,” Knowles told the Tallahassee Democrat. “But given the cards have been dealt, I’m just happy that I got an opportunity to help in any way that I can.” After winning back-to-back Southern Intercollegiate Athletic Conference Offensive Player of the Year awards and an NCAA Division II Black College Football National Championship at Albany State, Knowles made the no-brainer decision to transfer to FAMU to follow head coach Quinn Fordham Gray Sr. The Tampa native entered as the presumed starter for Gray’s first season at FAMU following their successful tenure together in the Peach State. But his time under center was cut short to two games . On Sept. 6, Knowles broke his right throwing-hand thumb in the Rattlers’ Orange Blossom Classic football game against South Carolina State. While attempting a pass, his hand hit off of a teammate’s helmet. The quarterback attempted to pop his thumb into place himself. FAMU trainers tried also to no avail. Knowles ran to the sideline, and then X-rays later revealed the severity of the injury that ended his season and ultimately his college football career. “They told me there were too many bones moving,” Knowles recalled the injury, “So we covered it up, walked back to the X-rays, and that’s when they told me what happened.” Knowles’ injury was the first domino to fall in a disastrous FAMU season as the Rattlers (2-8, 1-5 in SWAC) are on track for their fewest wins since 2015. “You know, I look at that kid every day and just think, ‘What if?’ But you can’t harp on things that happened in the past that aren’t in your favor,” Gray said of Knowles. “Losing a guy like that was tremendous for us in terms of our development this season.” FAMU QB Isaiah Knowles takes mentorship role for freshman Armond Parker After two starts in relief of Knowles, backup Dustin Fletcher suffered a similar throwing-hand thumb injury and has been out since mid-September. So, the Rattlers have turned to true freshman quarterback Armond Parker , who’s started six games this year fresh out of high school. Parker was an early FAMU enrollee, arriving on campus this past January for organized team activities and spring football training camp , wanting to learn everything from Knowles, who’s spent four years in Gray’s offensive system. They’ve “been attached at the hip” ever since, and Knowles has “been there every step of the way.” “It’s a testament to his character,” said FAMU running back Jamal Hailey . “Still waking up at five in the morning, showing up so he can be there so our freshman quarterback can be prepared week to week.” Knowles began watching games from the coach’s box for an aerial view of the offense. item.title: Man Utd open talks with Pochettino over replacing Carrick: reports
item.description: United States coach Mauricio Pochettino has experience of the Premier League from his time managing Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea (Omar Vega) Manchester United have opened talks with United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino about replacing Michael Carrick as manager, the BBC and other British media reported Wednesday. Carrick's position at Old Trafford has been the subject of intense speculation following United's worst start to a season in 40 years, leaving them languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after an eight-match winless run. He remains in post but it is believed Carrick's future will be decided at a meeting attended by influential shareholder Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox in Monaco on Wednesday. Although it is said that no final decision has been made, Berrada and Wilcox are reportedly leaning towards dismissing Carrick. Pochettino has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. United are understood to have spoken to the former Argentina defender about their managerial position on three previous occasions -- when Jose Mourinho was sacked in 2018, then in 2022 before the club appointed Erik ten Hag and again when the Dutchman was sacked in 2024. But it was only three months ago that Pochettino signed a contract extension to remain with the United States through to the 2030 World Cup and US Soccer would be due compensation should he move to Manchester, with the BBC saying the 54-year-old has a $10 million (£7.5 million) release clause. - Turbulent reign - Carrick was seen arriving at United's Carrington training ground on Wednesday but it appears to be only a matter of time before his turbulent reign comes to an end. The 45-year-old had been granted a stay of execution after he was widely expected to be axed in late October following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth. But United were beaten 2-0 at Chelsea, then scrambled a last-gasp 3-2 win against Roma in the Champions League after falling two goals down. It looked certain that former United and England midfielder Carrick would be on the way out when his team twice trailed by two goals against Aston Villa on Sunday. When United scored twice in stoppage-time to rescue an improbable 4-4 draw, it was interpreted as a positive sign for Carrick as the players were still fighting for him. But a change now appears likely. United have the rest of the two-week international break to resolve their managerial situation before returning to action at bitter rivals Liverpool on November 22. Carrick has presided over United's slide to 18th place -- their lowest position 10 games into a top-flight season since 1986/87 when they were 20th. He was hired on a permanent basis in the close-season after leading United to a third-place finish in the Premier League during his spell as interim boss. item.title: Today in Boston Celtics history: Greg Minor, Maurice King debut for Boston
item.description: Today in Boston Celtics history, Greg Minor made his debut for the storied ball club, the first tilt of a five-season stint with the team. An alumnus of the University of Louisville, where he put up 12.6 points and 5.6 rebounds per game and helped his team secure two trips to the Sweet 16 in the NCAA tournament, Minor ended up being selected by the Los Angeles Clippers with the 25th overall pick of the 1994 NBA draft without ever actually suiting up for them. The Georgia native was traded the day after the draft to the Indiana Pacers with Mark Jackson for Eric Piatkowski, Pooh Richardson, and Malik Sealy – and then was waived by the Pacers. He was then picked up by the Celtics as a free agent a few days later. Minor suited up for Boston for the first time in a 102-82 loss to the Houston Rockets, getting four minutes of floor time with no turnovers or fouls. He scored 2 points on 1-of-2 shooting and block a single shot for good measure for a respectable if unremarkable debut. Historic milestones It is also the date of Boston floor general Maurice King debuting for the Celtics in a 151-118 demolition of the (then) Cincinnati Royals (now, Sacramento Kings ) at the old Boston Garden in 1959. The Kansas product played 19 minutes and scored an impressive 10 points, 4 rebounds, and 2 assists. item.title: Family, football and legacy | Windthorst's Brock Belcher fueled by tradition
item.description: Cy Belcher never wanted his younger brother to be Windthorst's quarterback. It wasn't because Brock lacked the talent. In fact, it was quite the opposite. Even at a young age, he possessed the athleticism, instincts and natural ability that made him stand out amongst other "peewee" players. But Cy, a former player and now a quarterbacks coach at Windthorst, understood the expectations that came with leading one of the Wichita Falls area's most tradition-rich small-school football programs. "I didn't really want him to have to be the guy because of all the pressure that comes with that," Cy said. "I feel more nervous watching him now than I ever did playing because I want him to do so well." The original plan was for Brock to play receiver, a position he'd grown up playing alongside safety. But once Cy watched his younger brother throw the football, it became difficult to imagine him playing anything else. "After seeing him throw the ball and he just had great instincts, it was like, okay, I mean, he's kind of the guy," Cy said. What began as an unexpected position change has turned into one of the more remarkable quarterback careers in Windthorst — and Texas — high school football history. Now a senior, Brock has become one of the Red River area's most dynamic offensive players, combining a powerful arm and athleticism with a natural feel for the game. And while his Friday-night performances have made him stand out, the foundation of his success was built years earlier, with his father and older brother helping shape a player who once had no plans to become a quarterback. Brotherly building blocks Brock's path to becoming Windthorst's quarterback began with a state championship he watched from the stands. In 2020, the Trojans captured the Class 2A Division II state title with Cy playing quarterback. Brock was in sixth grade, watching his older brother accomplish something he and his classmates would spend the next several years frothing at the mouth over. "I realized a long time ago in 2020 [that I wanted to play quarterback] whenever I watched that happen," Brock said. "I knew I wanted to do this, and I wanted to do it to the best of my ability." Shortly after the state championship, the two brothers began lifting weights together at 4:30 a.m. each day. What started as offseason training eventually became the foundation of Brock's development at a position he'd never expected to play. And when the youth football team had no established quarterback in his age group, he was moved behind center to fill the gap, with Cy taking on the responsibility of teaching him the position. "He has taught me just about everything I know," Brock said with a grin. "He's a very smart guy, but he won't tell that to you." item.title: “There Might Be Something Subtle”: Ohio State OC Addresses Jeremiah Smith’s Problem After 32-Minute Target Drought Against Oregon
item.description: Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) celebrates a touchdown during the NCAA football game against the Ohio Bobcats at Ohio Stadium © Reuters Ohio State’s offensive struggles have become increasingly difficult to ignore after back-to-back losses. They lost to USC and, last week, to Oregon. One of the biggest concerns about the team’s play is wide receiver Jeremiah Smith’s limited involvement. Despite being one of the greatest players in college football, he went through an extended stretch without a target during the Buckeyes’ 41-28 defeat to Oregon. Jeremiah recorded seven receptions for 133 yards and a touchdown, averaging 19 yards per catch. However, after recording his third reception with 2:59 remaining in the first quarter, the wide receiver did not receive another target until just 15 seconds remained in the third quarter. That amounted to 32 minutes and 44 seconds without a target. During his press conference, Arthur Smith was asked whether he keeps track of stretches when Jeremiah isn’t involved in the offense. “Oh, absolutely. And, you know, there are different reasons. You know, obviously, he’s one of the top, most-targeted players in all of football. You know, football, certainly college football, and receptions. That’s always the argument. There are certain things where you try to make sure he gets the ball, and there might be something subtle that happens that causes it not to go there, whether it’s coverage or there was a breakdown somewhere else,” Arthur Smith said. He said that the coaching staff does try to find ways to get the ball to Jeremiah, but defensive coverage and unexpected breakdowns change the intended play. Jeremiah Smith Faces Criticism After Ohio State’s Loss While the offensive game plan has attracted criticism, FOX analyst Joel Klatt believes Jeremiah also needs to take responsibility for his performance. Klatt pointed to several instances where the receiver was slow off the line. “Even Jeremiah didn’t play great all game. There were times when he was slow off the line of scrimmage. He didn’t win the one-on-one ball down into the end zone early in the game,” he said on “The Joel Klatt Show.” “He was late out of his breaks. There were times when the routes weren’t being run, I’ll be honest, full speed. And that was a bit alarming to see for me, cause I’ve come to see a standard on film from number four at Ohio State that is higher than what was on film on Saturday’s game,” Klatt added. Klatt acknowledged that the offensive scheme deserves significant blame, arguing that Ohio State lacked creativity in getting its best playmaker involved. With three games remaining in the regular season, the Buckeyes need to address the disconnect ASAP. Getting Jeremiah Smith consistently involved would be crucial if Ohio State hopes to turn its season around now. That works out to roughly one goal for every five shots, highlighting the quality of the team's attacking play and finishing. item.title: Dion Beljo: Man United’s pursuit of Dinamo striker under threat from Newcastle United, Leeds United
item.description: Dion Beljo: Man United’s pursuit of Dinamo striker under threat from Newcastle United, Leeds United Manchester United are in troubled waters following a poor start to the season, which has seen them drop into the relegation zone after 10 games. The Red Devils have won just one of those matches, the fewest among the 20 teams, and have scored 14 goals in the league this season. Goalscoring appears to be a major problem for Michael Carrick’s team, especially since Benjamin Sesko has struggled to stay fit, managing just 206 minutes of first-team football across six games. The Slovenian is out of action until at least January, leaving United short in the No. 9 position. With Joshua Zirkzee failing to impress, the Red Devils are likely to pursue a new striker once the transfer window opens in January. A recent report relayed by The Peoples Person suggests that they have identified Dinamo Zagreb striker Dion Beljo as a possible target. A goalscoring phenomenon Beljo joined Dinamo Zagreb last summer and was outstanding last season, scoring 38 goals and registering six assists in 48 games. The 24-year-old has continued that golden run this campaign as well, and now has 19 goals and nine assists in 20 appearances. Beljo is a towering centre-forward who can dominate opposition defenders and makes intelligent runs to split open the backline. He has an eye for goal and excels in link-up play, and is exactly the kind of player United lack in their squad at the moment. The Croatian was on song against Sunderland at the Stadium of Light last week in the Europa League, helping his team secure a 2-0 victory. It now appears that his efforts have also turned heads at several clubs in the English top flight. United face competition for Beljo According to TEAMtalk , Newcastle United and Leeds United have stepped up their pursuit of Beljo. The report states: “Newcastle and Leeds were both represented on Wearside to watch Beljo in action against Sunderland, giving them another opportunity to assess his performances against Premier League opposition.” The report confirms that Beljo has also turned heads at Sunderland following his impressive outing last week, while United continue to keep him under close watch. It continues: “Manchester United, Tottenham Hotspur and Everton are also understood to have been tracking his progress, while Brighton and Brentford have previously checked on his situation.” All signs indicate that the Red Devils will not have a free run at the explosive Croatian, who looks certain to be on his way in January. item.title: Milan Prepare Renewal for Starlet After Brighton Links
item.description: Milan Prepare Renewal for Starlet After Brighton Links Milan and Ruben Amorim have been rewarded for trusting Alphadjo Cisse and rejecting the offers for him last summer. Brighton have shown interest lately, but the Rossoneri have every intention of keeping the starlet and want to extend his contract, Matteo Moretto reports (via Tribuna ). PSV targeted the talent last summer, and he had a host of opportunities to leave on loan. However, the coach insisted on keeping him in the squad while they were dealing with a few injuries and late returns after the World Cup. He’s been an integral part of the rotation. Cisse leads Milan in scoring, having hit the net 8 times in 13 matches, thanks to a hat-trick against RB Salzburg and a brace versus Bologna. He’s already under contract until 2030. However, the plan is to quickly reward him for his growth. He’ll likely debut with Italy in the upcoming UEFA Nations League contests. The Rossoneri are reaping the rewards of a gamble by their ousted director, Igli Tare, in this case. He snapped up the starlet from Verona for €8M when he was still in the youth academy. He got off to a great start at Catanzaro in 2025/2026 too. Though, his season was cut short by a serious thigh injury. Our Take on Milan and Cisse He has produced at every level, but his acquisition looked like just a way to help Verona financially at the time, as he wasn’t worth that price tag. Instead, it turned out to be a great forward-thinking investment that should inform other teams as well, rather than constantly searching for short-term improvements. He’s not going anywhere, and his chemistry and compatibility with their big dogs are quickly improving.

item.description: Paul Scholes has made himself look stupid with latest bizarre criticism of struggling Man United Former Manchester United midfielder Paul Scholes has criticised the team’s habit of performing laps of honour after matches. Struggling United are enduring a dreadful season so far, with the club in a state of turmoil greater than ever before. Sunday’s dramatic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa left United in 18th place, a position that is largely new and unfathomable for them. Yet the performances and results make clear this reality is not shocking. United have won just once in the Premier League this season: the 5-2 triumph over Ipswich Town in August. The Red Devils have also recorded five draws and four defeats. A meagre eight points from 10 games has left Michael Carrick on the brink of dismissal. An announcement could come as early as today, following the outcome of a Monaco meeting between Sir Jim Ratcliffe and club chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox. While Carrick has taken most of the flak for United’s plight, the top brass have hardly escaped scrutiny for their repeated poor decisions and dreadful work in the transfer market. But Ratcliffe still retains faith in Berrada and Wilcox . The pair will not lose their jobs. Following the final whistle against Villa, the United players circled Old Trafford applauding the supporters. They received a mixed reception but were less fortunate against Bournemouth, when the fans booed them loudly. Speaking on The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast , Scholes took aim at United’s regular laps of honour. Scholes’ view The club legend said, “I tell you one thing they need to do, stop doing these laps of honour after every game.” “What the f–k! It’s so bad.” He added, “Jesus, it’s embarrassing. Every game’s like the last game of the season. Just get off!” Scholes may deride United’s players for applauding the fans, but an argument can be made that they are simply thanking the supporters, particularly after what they have had to endure this season. Simply walking down the tunnel would be the easier option, yet their acknowledgement must surely mean something. United are next in action on November 22 when they go away to Liverpool.

Atletico Madrid and Chelsea are both reportedly circling the Spain international ahead of January. Diego Simeone is said to be eager to bring Zubimendi back to Spain, while Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso is also reportedly interested. Midfielder frustrated by constant transfer speculation The £60 million signing from Real Sociedad admitted that the constant swirl of transfer gossip has caught him off guard. Speaking to Marca , he expressed a desire for more caution regarding published rumours. "To be honest, I’m sometimes surprised by the press too," Zubimendi explained. "I understand that the winter transfer window is approaching and rumours can surface, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish. Arteta outlined clear plan for the season Zubimendi's Arsenal career started brightly 18 months ago, but fatigue allowed Myles Lewis-Skelly to take his place late last season. "I spoke with Mikel at the beginning of the season," he said. "He warned me that there were new signings and that there would be playing time for everyone. And here we are, fighting for it. item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. item.title: Rio Ngumoha says he can win the Ballon d'Or after Harry Kane's triumph: 'I think I can do it'
item.description: Rio Ngumoha says he can win the Ballon d'Or after Harry Kane's triumph: 'I think I can do it' Rio Ngumoha believes Harry Kane 's Ballon d'Or win has opened the door for young English players and has backed himself as a future winner. Kane claimed the award on October 26, beating Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal to become the first Englishman in 25 years to be named the world's best player. The England captain is also set to break his country's all-time appearance record with a 126th cap against Croatia on Thursday. Ngumoha, 18, is with the squad for the Nations League double-header against Croatia and Spain. With Bukayo Saka injured, the Liverpool winger is competing with Morgan Rogers for a role on the right. He was part of Thomas Tuchel's pre-World Cup camp in Florida and has since made two substitute appearances against the Czech Republic. Training alongside Kane, he said, showed him what it takes to reach the top. "When I first came, I was a bit shy, so I was keeping myself to myself," Ngumoha said. "But then they got me in the group, and just watching him train, watching all the players train, but especially him, the finishing drills that you see. You can see why he won (the Ballon d'Or) and why he's known as the best striker, best player in the world. Definitely an inspiration to me, but just to every young player and probably every England player as well. He's a top guy." The winger also credited Raheem Sterling, who offered him advice during his time at Chelsea before he joined Liverpool in 2024. "Raheem Sterling pulled me to the side a couple of times and told me he could see I had talent but I should never zone out in the game, and I should always be in the game," he said. "The best players are always in the game in the last minutes. If you look at him and Mohamed Salah, they're always there until the crucial moments. Learning from them was important." 'Everyone's seen one of us win the Ballon d'Or' For Ngumoha, the significance of Kane's win stretches beyond the Bayern Munich striker himself. He said Kane's win has shown young English talent that they can be considered the world's best and believes he is capable of following in the 33-year-old's footsteps. "Harry Kane winning the Ballon d'Or is definitely a big, big thing, him being known as the best player in the world. It's also helped English football now because everyone's seen one of us win the Ballon d'Or. It is definitely encouraging many more people to want to be definitively known as the best player in the world. For me, I would like to achieve it and I think I can do it."

item.title: Tearful Smith switches allegiance to Netherlands
item.description: Tatjana Smith won a gold and silver medal at each of the past two Olympics [Getty Images] South Africa's most decorated Olympian Tatjana Smith was in tears as she announced that she has switched allegiance to the Netherlands. The 29-year-old won four Olympic breaststroke medals, including two golds, before retiring after the Paris 2024 Games. She came out of retirement in September and hopes to compete in the 50m breaststroke as the event makes its Olympic debut at the 2028 Games in Los Angeles. Smith, whose maiden name was Schoenmaker, wiped away tears as she read a letter addressed to South Africa, saying that "dreams can change as we grow". Smith has dual citizenship because her father is Dutch. She said she has "always been Dutch and South African" and that this is an opportunity to "explore another part of my identity and heritage that I've never experienced through sport". She said it also offers her "greater high-performance support and the potential to build a more sustainable career" because the "financial and practical challenges of swimming were among the reasons my previous career became difficult to sustain". Smith has previously said that financial worries, which included a dispute with Swimming South Africa over prize money, contributed to her decision to step away from the sport. Swimming South Africa has been approached for comment. Smith won four world and Commonwealth gold medals between 2018 and 2023. She won gold in the 200m breaststroke and 100m silver at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, before adding 100m gold and 200m silver in 2024. "Representing South Africa was a childhood dream come true, and it's a chapter I will always look back on with immense pride and gratitude," she said on social media. "The people, the memories and everything we achieved together will always be part of me. But dreams can change as we grow. "This next chapter is about embracing another part of who I am, falling in love with the journey and discovering what more I'm capable of. "I'm excited for what lies ahead, and I truly hope you'll continue to be part of the journey with me." Smith, who said she will continue to live and train in South Africa, is set to represent the Netherlands for the first time at the short course World Championships from 1-6 December. She acknowledged that her switch "may disappoint or break the hearts" of some supporters. The Ministry of Sport, Arts and Culture in South Africa said it was aware of the "problems at Swimming South Africa". "The country was delighted to see her return to the pool, but South Africa does not own her," a statement read. "Tatjana's choice belongs to her and it should not be turned into a political weapon." Gayton McKenzie, Minister of Sports, Arts and Culture, said: "Every medal, every record and every anthem she gave us belongs to our history forever. We now have to share her with the Netherlands." item.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images Paul George has found new life since joining the Boston Celtics as part of the Jaylen Brown trade, and he believes they’ve done what the Philadelphia 76ers couldn’t. item.title: Real Madrid legend Toni Kroos blown away by Barcelona superstar’s performance against Atletico Madrid
item.description: Real Madrid legend Toni Kroos blown away by Barcelona superstar’s performance against Atletico Madrid Real Madrid legend Toni Kroos has never been shy about speaking his mind in the media, either during his playing days or since retiring. The German midfielder’s best quality has always been his willingness to call a spade a spade, and he has now waxed lyrical about Barcelona star Lamine Yamal’s performance against Atletico. Atletico lost 2-1 to Hansi Flick’s Barça , missing the chance to go top of La Liga . Kroos amazed by Lamine Yamal’s performance Speaking on his podcast Einfach mal Luppen , the German was amazed by what the Spanish teenager produced on the night. “Lamine Yamal’s first 25 minutes were absolutely exceptional,” Kroos remarked, highlighting the teenager’s extraordinary influence during the opening stages. Toni Kroos was full of praise for Lamine Yamal’s performance against Atletico Madrid. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The former Madrid midfielder was particularly impressed by Yamal’s ability to manufacture opportunities without relying on his team-mates to provide favourable situations. “Every dangerous Barcelona attack seemed to come through him,” he explained. “He was creating those advantages himself, beating opponents and producing chances through his own individual brilliance.” Kroos felt that Yamal’s confidence was so overwhelming that the youngster appeared capable of taking complete responsibility for helping Barça stage a comeback. “At one point, you could almost imagine him telling his teammates: ‘Just give me the ball. We’ll turn this game around,'” he added. Rare praise from a Real Madrid legend While there is no doubt that Lamine Yamal is an excellent footballer, it is rare to see someone associated with Real Madrid be so effusive in their praise for a Barcelona star. Even when there is mutual admiration, modern footballers are increasingly media-trained to avoid expressing it publicly. Toni Kroos has always been very candid throughout his career. (Photo by Lars Baron/Getty Images) However, Kroos has never been that kind of person, and his praise for the 19-year-old Barcelona winger seems very genuine. Kroos understands better than most what kind of mentality it takes to pull off comebacks in important games. Against Atletico, Barcelona never let their heads drop, and one of the main reasons was the conviction with which Yamal played. The numbers may show only the assist he provided for Fermin’s goal in the second half, but his performance was about much more than that. Real Madrid have increasingly found Lamine to be one of their biggest headaches in El Clasico , and it remains to be seen how the Barça teenager’s evolution pans out.

The generational goaltender consistently achieved excellence and pushed his body to the limit for his teammates and supporters. Although knee injuries shortened what is still a Hall of Fame career, his dedication to the Habs is beyond doubt. Just look at what transpired in the Bell Centre before Tuesday night’s battle versus the Minnesota Wild. item.title: Man Utd open talks with Pochettino as Carrick faces sack
item.description: Man Utd open talks with Pochettino as Carrick faces sack Manchester United have reportedly opened talks with Mauricio Pochettino over becoming their next head coach, with Michael Carrick facing an increasingly uncertain future at Old Trafford. United’s senior leadership is expected to discuss Carrick’s position at a meeting in Monaco on Wednesday, involving co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox. The latter two are expected to recommend a change in the dugout following the club’s disappointing start to the season. Pochettino has emerged as the leading candidate to replace Carrick, with reports indicating that United have held discussions with the former Tottenham and Chelsea manager. The Times reports that the club are negotiating personal terms, although United have yet to formally approach the United States Soccer Federation over his release. Man Utd open talks with Mauricio Pochettino as Michael Carrick faces sack The 54-year-old only extended his contract as USA head coach in August, committing his future to the national team until 2030. His agreement reportedly includes a release clause worth around $10 million (£7.5m), which could facilitate a return to club management. Pochettino is no stranger to United’s managerial search. The club previously considered appointing him following Jose Mourinho’s departure in 2018, before choosing Erik ten Hag in 2022 and again after the Dutchman’s dismissal in 2024. His Premier League experience includes spells at Southampton and Tottenham, where he guided Spurs to the 2019 Champions League final. He subsequently managed Paris Saint-Germain before taking charge of Chelsea for the 2023-24 campaign. Carrick’s position has deteriorated sharply after United slipped into 18th place in the Premier League table. The club have managed just one league victory in their opening 10 matches and have not won since August, marking their worst start to a top-flight season at this stage since 1986-87. However, United have not officially confirmed Carrick’s departure, and the Monaco meeting is expected to determine the next step. The club must also consider the implications of attempting to prise Pochettino away from his international commitments. item.title: How much Manchester United will pay USMNT for Mauricio Pochettino
item.description: Photo by David Berding/USSF/Getty Images Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United is picking up steam on Wednesday morning, as the USMNT head coach lines up his exit from the role. It has been reported by reliable soccer journalist David Ornstein that Man United are finalising a deal to appoint Pochettino as their potential replacement, should they sack Michael Carrick. It is claimed that terms are being discussed with the Argentine’s camp. Pochettino is currently working with the USMNT during the international break, but his exit from the role looks like a matter of when rather than if. Although it is stated that United have not yet contacted the US over the potential appointment of Pochettino, a deal would be easy to pull off. With Pochettino looking set to return to the Premier League, United would be required to pay the USMNT given the 54-year-old is still under contract. Man United prepared to pay USMNT compensation to appoint Mauricio Pochettino Pochettino signed a new contract with the USMNT following the World Cup earlier this year, but a simple clause was included for allowing him to leave for a European club should the compensation figure be paid. A report from The Telegraph in England has revealed that a fee of just under $10m will be paid by United to the USMNT to release Pochettino from his contract. It is also claimed that United could wait to make a formal move until after the US’s playoff games. The USMNT play Haiti on Saturday and then next Wednesday in a two-legged quarter-final in the Concacaf Nations League. However, it is stated in the report that Pochettino is keen to make the move to Old Trafford. Although this is far from what the USMNT will have wanted after securing Pochettino down to a new deal in the summer, there is an upside to bringing in around $10m in compensation as opposed to potentially losing him for nothing earlier in the year after the World Cup.
